title: Make create_group_chat all-or-nothing
problem: create_group_chat inserts a chat, its memberships and a first message, and commits after every step. When one member id is unknown, the caller gets an IntegrityError, but the chat and the earlier memberships are already committed: a half-created group. Refactor it so the whole operation is one transaction, and so repeated ids don't break it.
requirements: Edit only groups.py; keep the function's signature and return value
All writes of one call happen in one transaction: committed together on success, rolled back together on any exception
The exception still reaches the caller (don't swallow it)
After a failure, no transaction is left open on the connection and the connection can be used again
Each user becomes a member once, even if listed twice or if the creator is also in member_ids
A blank title raises ValueError before anything is written
contract: create_group_chat(conn: sqlite3.Connection, title: str, creator_id: int, member_ids: list[int], now: str) -> int   # the new chat's id; conn uses the default transaction mode
expectedBehavior: create_group_chat(conn, 'weekend', 1, [2, 3], NOW) returns 5 and another connection sees the chat, 3 memberships and the message; with member_ids [2, 999] it raises sqlite3.IntegrityError and every table looks exactly as before, on both connections
edgeCases: Unknown member id after valid ones: nothing written, error raised
member_ids repeats an id or contains the creator
member_ids is empty: a chat with just the creator
Title with surrounding spaces is stored stripped; a blank title writes nothing
A successful call right after a failed one works and is committed
hints: Conceptual: every conn.commit() in the middle is a point after which a later failure can no longer be undone. An atomic operation commits exactly once, at the end, and rolls back if anything before that raises.

Specific: remove the intermediate commits and put all the INSERTs inside one `with conn:` block. It commits when the block finishes normally and rolls back (then re-raises) when anything inside raises. For duplicates, build the list of people without repeats before the transaction.

Implementation: people = dict.fromkeys([creator_id, *member_ids]) keeps the first occurrence of each id, in order. Then: with conn: insert the chat, loop over people inserting memberships, insert the message. Return chat_id after the block.
evaluation: Exactly one transaction per call, with no commit() in the middle
Errors propagate to the caller; nothing catches and hides them
Validation that needs no database happens before the transaction starts
